name: Kulintangan
description: The melodic centre of the ensemble: a row of bossed gongs traditionally made from brass, although iron may now be used because brass is difficult to obtain. The interview records nine kettle gongs, but this count is KIV and still requires confirmation. Skilled makers were identified in Matunggong, Kudat, and Kota Belud.

name: Agung
description: Suspended gongs that support, answer and signal within the ensemble. The interview distinguishes agung buah (also described as canang or bell), agung sambut, and agung tawag-tawag. Tawag means “to call” in Suluk; this rapidly played part was historically used to summon the community or signal an emergency. Traditionally made from brass, with iron now also used.

name: Tambul
description: The drum that drives the rhythm alongside the gongs. Earlier tambul used a refined goatskin head, a wooden frame, a brass or iron body, and a coarse sack-like tension rope. Hard, termite-resistant wood such as belian or ipil was used for the beater. A shop-bought drum may be substituted today.
